cohort: Pregnant women who gave birth in a large hospital network in Melbourne, Australia, between 2016 and 2022.
finding: Prepregnancy and pregnancy cardiometabolic risk factors and conditions, pregnancy and birth complications, and obstetric interventions significantly increased over a 7-year period, although offspring complications like special care admissions and prematurity decreased.
mod_finding: Caesarean delivery rates increased from 28.5% to 37.6% over the 7-year study period, but during the COVID-19 lockdown, the odds of induced birth increased by 8.0% while the odds of caesarean section decreased by 5.0%.
